stem: Gallium is a metal in Group 13 of the Periodic Table.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: There are two stable isotopes of gallium, $^{69}\text{Ga}$ and $^{71}\text{Ga}$.
parts.text: State, with reference to subatomic particles, how the isotopes $^{69}\text{Ga}$ and $^{71}\text{Ga}$ differ from each other.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State what further information is needed to calculate the relative atomic mass of gallium.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Gallium and its compounds show similar properties to aluminium and its compounds. Gallium reacts with excess chlorine to form gallium trichloride.
parts.text:
At $500^{\circ}\text{C}$, gallium trichloride is a gas.

Suggest the type of attraction that exists at $500^{\circ}\text{C}$

• between atoms within a gallium trichloride molecule

• between gallium trichloride molecules.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
When gallium trichloride is cooled a solid, $\text{Ga}_2\text{Cl}_6$, forms.

Suggest the name of the attraction formed between two gallium trichloride molecules to form $\text{Ga}_2\text{Cl}_6$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Gallium metal reacts rapidly when exposed to air. A white solid layer is formed on its surface.
parts.text: Suggest an equation to describe the reaction occurring when gallium metal is exposed to air.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The table gives the formula of each gallium-containing product formed when gallium oxide reacts separately with hot aqueous hydrochloric acid and hot aqueous sodium hydroxide.

|  | formula of gallium-containing product |
| :--- | :--- |
| hot aqueous hydrochloric acid | $\text{GaCl}_3$ |
| hot aqueous sodium hydroxide | $\text{NaGa(OH)}_4$ |

Give the name of the type of behaviour shown by gallium oxide in these reactions.
